title: [CQ-RF06b] VS Code protected daemon spawn
description:
Objective: under the protected profile, the VS Code extension starts the Moe daemon only from the runtime installed with the extension. This mirrors JetBrains MoeDaemonSupervisor.protectedDaemonCommand / protectedDaemonEnvironment / protectedCommandOrRefuse. Split out of CQ-RF06 (task-98ffe33f448746e6bc802db0b5624fd0) by architect-bd1eb82d on 2026-10-30 to keep each diff under the 400-LOC review cap. RF06 lands the shared policy as exported functions in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts: runtimeProfile (strict, fail-closed, session pin), comparablePath/isWithin, installedRoot(extensionPath) = <extensionPath>/bundled and installedArtifact. This row consumes them in the same file.

Deliverable: when runtimeProfile(projectPath) is 'protected', MoeDaemonClient.startDaemon:
1. Selects the daemon with installedArtifact(installedRoot, 'daemon/index.js', projectPath). resolveGlobalConfigDaemonPath and any project copy are never consulted.
2. Selects node as an absolute, real, regular file outside the project (a mirror of JetBrains installedExecutable). It tries, in this order:
   - MOE_NODE_COMMAND;
   - on non-Windows, ~/.local/share/moe/node/current/bin/node;
   - an in-process lookup of node or node.exe over PATH entries that are absolute and outside the project (never a bare name resolved by spawn);
   - on Windows, the resolveNodeExecutable candidates (ProgramFiles, ProgramFiles(x86), LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\nodejs, LOCALAPPDATA\nvm\current, APPDATA\nvm).
3. Spawns [node, daemon, 'start', '--project', projectPath] with cwd = the installed daemon's directory. The env drops NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH, and PATH (matched case-insensitively on Windows) keeps only absolute entries outside the project.
4. Refuses instead of falling back: any rejection starts nothing, logs the reason and shows `Protected execution profile: <reason>. Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used.`
5. The legacy profile is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Out of scope:
- Running-daemon provenance (JetBrains activationRefusal, spawn records, RF03 replacement). VS Code under protected still connects to an existing daemon.json daemon. Node has no portable process start-time API, so this stays a known gap, recorded for CQ-RF07.
- Persistent state, JetBrains changes, .moe edits, enabling verified-local.

Constraint: five test harnesses (daemon-start, daemon-json-cap, approval-paths, plan-approval-client, settings-wire) transpile MoeDaemonClient.ts alone with a closed require shim. Add no new local runtime import to MoeDaemonClient.ts.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile

Shown by tests in a new moe-vscode/tests/*.test.cjs.

Under the protected profile, a missing installed daemon, or no acceptable node, spawns nothing, shows the 'Protected execution profile: … Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used.' refusal, and never consults the global-config daemon. Shown by tests.
The legacy profile behaves exactly as before: the existing daemon-start tests pass unchanged.

implementationPlan.note:
Reopen 1 (QA reject: Windows root-relative PATH). RED tests added to tests/protected-daemon-spawn.test.cjs:
(1) a cross-platform predicate test for the new isFullyQualified(p, windows). '\x', '/x', 'C:x' and '\\' are rejected; 'C:\x', 'c:/x', '\\srv\sh', '//srv/sh' and '\\?\C:\x' are accepted; there are posix rows too.
(2) a win32-only test (explicit skip elsewhere). The rooted backslash and slash spellings of the C: temp project and of an outside dir are refused by isOutsideProject; a rooted MOE_NODE_COMMAND is refused by installedExecutable; protectedDaemonEnvironment drops all of them but keeps the drive-qualified outside dir and its \\?\ device spelling. Outside-dir rooted forms make this a wiring regression whatever the host drive; the project form is QA's exact D:-cwd/C:-temp repro.
(3) The protectedPathEntries row now expects the validated spelling only. Edge-quote entries ("x, x', x", 'x, and space-padded quoted) are dropped. I verified empirically on Windows node v24.16.0 that libuv's PATH search strips a leading or trailing ' or " (PATH=C:\Windows\System32' still runs whoami), so C:\proj' searched as C:\proj passed validation.
RED evidence: Linux 19 tests, 16 pass / 2 fail (as-written quoted entries retained; isFullyQualified missing) / 1 win-only skip (/tmp/rf06b-reopen-red-linux.log). Native Windows 19 tests, 15 pass / 3 fail, including QA's case: \Users\Yaron\AppData\Local\Temp\moe-rf06b-*\project is accepted, true !== false (/tmp/rf06b-reopen-red-windows.log).
The exported isFullyQualified is a small approvedScope addition driven by the QA fix. Peer dirty paths untouched.

Reopen-1 fix in MoeDaemonClient.ts, +11/-5:
- New export isFullyQualified(p, windows = host win32), checked against the HOST platform. On Windows it accepts only drive-qualified `C:\`/`C:/` or `\\`/`//` + non-separator (UNC and \\?\ device forms), the same set Java NIO's WindowsPath.isAbsolute accepts in JetBrains. POSIX keeps posix.isAbsolute.
- isOutsideProject (QA line 256) and installedExecutable (QA line 227 audit) now require it. A rooted MOE_NODE_COMMAND gets the existing 'node executable is not an absolute path' refusal.
- protectedPathEntries now returns the validated unquoted spelling, not the as-written one, and drops entries that end in ' or ". A leading quote already fails qualification. libuv strips an edge quote, verified on Windows node v24.16.0.
- nodeOnProtectedPath joins the validated entry. protectedDaemonEnvironment dedupes after filtering, and its blank filter was redundant.
- Legacy code is untouched and there are no new imports.

Test tweak: the predicate cases are folded into the for loop and the duplicate comment is dropped, to save lines (behaviour unchanged).

GREEN:
- protected-daemon-spawn.test.cjs: Linux 19 tests, 18 pass, 1 win-only skip; native Windows 18 pass, 1 inherited symlink skip.
- Full Linux npm test: 286 tests, 285 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip.
- QA's repro logic, pointed at the working-tree source (D:\rf06b-worker-scratch\repro-worktree.cjs): exit 0, accepted=false, filteredPATH has only the node dir (/tmp/rf06b-reopen-qa-repro.log).

Mutation: 10/10 assertion-killed, with a clean baseline on both platforms. The mutants: isAbsolute in isOutsideProject (win), in installedExecutable (win), no edge-quote filter, as-written retention, drop UNC, accept C:x, host default false (win), accept rooted, double-quote-only, single-quote-only.

- (a) The protected dispatch returns before resolveBundledDaemonPath, resolveGlobalConfigDaemonPath and resolveDaemonRuntime. A bare or rooted node is refused.
- (b) The first found candidate is validated. A Windows fallback under a rooted env var (ProgramFiles=\x) is now refused rather than skipped.
- (c) The env is a `{...env}` copy (tests assert the input is unchanged).
- (d) Case-insensitive NODE_* and a single PATH spelling are unchanged.
- (e) cwd is the installed daemon dir.
- (f) Legacy bytes are untouched (D7 and the 5 harnesses pass).
- (g) The UI refusal strings are fixed and paths go to the log only.

Reopen specifics:
- isFullyQualified is pure and its default is evaluated per call, so the vm `process` works.
- Empty/NUL inputs give false.
- `\\?\` and `\\.\` spellings of the project are still refused through comparablePath's device-prefix strip and realpath.
- Trailing-space and trailing-dot spellings of an EXISTING project dir are refused through realpath.
- The concurrency guard is unchanged: selection is synchronous before startInProgress is set.
The only edit in this step is doc wording: `C:\` and `\\` forms qualify with either slash.
Theoretical, pre-existing and shared with JetBrains, not fixed here: a not-yet-existing PATH leaf under an aliased ancestor (a symlink, an 8.3 name, a Windows trailing-dot/space segment, or an admin-share UNC to the project) is compared only lexically, because realpath of the leaf is ENOENT. It needs the user's own PATH spelled that way plus later creation inside the project, which is the same out-of-model creation race.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: This row was split from RF06 to stay under the 400-LOC review cap. The policy lives in MoeDaemonClient.ts (RF06's decision), because five vm harnesses transpile that file alone with a closed require shim. A separate module or extension.ts injection was rejected: the import breaks the harnesses, and an unwired client would fail open. --host 0.0.0.0 is omitted because VS Code has no WSL agent toggle. planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Legacy startDaemon picks bundled, then the global-config daemon, and node from resolveDaemonRuntime (MOE_NODE_COMMAND, else the managed node on non-Windows, else a bare 'node'). It spawns detached with stdio ignore. ensureDaemonRunning passes 'init' when .moe is missing. Under protected, .moe/project.json exists or a session pin holds, and JetBrains always uses 'start'. JetBrains daemonPath prepends node's dir and appends the bootstrap dirs, then protectedDaemonEnvironment filters PATH to absolute non-project entries.
planningNotes.risks:
- Windows env-key casing: a spread copy of process.env is case-sensitive. JetBrains hit a duplicate PATH/Path spelling that broke git, so keep exactly one spelling.
- The macOS tmpdir realpath differs from its path, so tests must compare realpaths.
- The non-Windows fixed candidates (/usr/bin/node and others) exist on CI hosts. Tests that need a 'nothing found' answer must use windows=true units (D5), not the real filesystem.
- RF06 must have landed: this task depends on it, and both edit the same file.
